basis: Inherited disruption of gluconeogenesis; no additional organ damage is common across this heterogeneous group.
Nonsyndromic X-linked intellectual disability; developmental impairment defines the disease.
Extraskeletal osteosarcoma originates in the liver; osteoid production does not establish skeletal involvement.
Structural rupture of an intrahepatic or extrahepatic bile duct.
Congenital pituitary ACTH deficiency causes adrenal insufficiency; hypoglycemic seizures do not establish lasting brain damage; hepatitis occurs in 5-29%.
Predisposition primarily to breast and ovarian cancer; susceptibility alone does not establish organ damage, including pancreatic damage.
Myoepithelial soft-tissue tumor typically occupying subfascial or subcutaneous tissues of the extremities.
Lysosomal leukodystrophy damages central and peripheral nerves; visual impairment and sensorineural hearing impairment are each reported in 80-99%.
Macular and central cone degeneration causes impaired acuity and central scotoma in 6/6 patients.
Proximal bicarbonate wasting causes metabolic acidosis; cataract, glaucoma and keratopathy occur in 3/3, as does intellectual disability.
Mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation defect; developmental/intellectual impairment and myopathy each reported in 3/8 (38%); ocular findings 2/8 are below threshold.
Hyperplastic epithelial polyp arising mainly in gastric or colonic mucosa.
Vitamin deficiency disrupts metabolic homeostasis; specific organ injuries vary by vitamin and do not apply across the umbrella.
Neuroblastoma originates in the adrenal medulla; metastatic involvement is not established as common enough for additional labels.
Microcephaly and severe developmental/intellectual impairment define the syndrome; scoliosis occurs in 30-79%; characteristic cry alone does not establish airway damage.
Acquired ACTH deficiency with autoimmunity reported in 80-99%; associated autoimmune diagnoses are separate diseases; gastrointestinal symptoms do not establish tissue damage.
Organic aciduria, neurodevelopmental disease and neutropenia define the syndrome; cataracts occur in 80-99%. Renal cysts/nephrocalcinosis (80-99%) omitted under the four-axis cap.
Early-onset epilepsy is a disorder of brain function; no shared additional organ injury is established.
Inflammatory hypophysitis with extensive pituitary necrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltration.
Immune-mediated lymphocytic inflammation and fibrosis of the breast; breast has no anatomical axis, and associated diabetes is a separate disease.
Primordial skeletal dysplasia with defining nail dysplasia and hypotrichosis; global developmental delay reported in 2/5 (40%); diabetes occurs in 5-29%.
Coffin-Siris neurodevelopmental, skeletal and hair/nail phenotype; hearing impairment in 3/4 (75%). Visual impairment (2/3) and cleft palate (2/4) omitted under four-axis cap.
Purely psychiatric mood disorder; no qualifying direct organ damage is part of its definition.
Platelet granule and aggregation disorder with thrombocytopenia and bleeding.
Extensive myelinated peripapillary retinal nerve fibers; the optic nerve and retinal structures belong to the ocular axis.
